title: Everything you need to know about the A75 transitional open work permit in Canada
excerpt: In the current panorama of Canadian immigration, the A75 transitional open work permit is an innovative solution for candidates for permanent…
html:
In the current panorama of Canadian immigration, the A75 transitional open work permit is an innovative solution for candidates for permanent residency in certain economic immigration categories. It is specifically designed to offer greater flexibility to individuals awaiting permanent status in Canada, enabling them to work for any employer without the need for a Labour Market Impact Assessment (LMIA). Designed to ease the transition to permanent residency, the A75 permit recognizes the vital contribution of foreign workers to the Canadian economy.

What is an A75 transitional open work permit?

The A75 Transitional Open Work Permit is a specific category of Canadian work permit under the International Mobility Program. This permit is designed to offer greater flexibility to applicants for permanent residence in Canada who apply through certain categories of economic immigration. Unlike closed work permits, which are tied to a specific employer, the A75 permit allows its holder to work for any employer in Canada without requiring a Labour Market Impact Assessment (LMI). The A75 Transitional Open Work Permit is particularly valuable for applicants who need to maintain their employment and legal status in Canada while their application for permanent residence is being processed.

Who is eligible to apply for an A75 transitional open work permit?

To be eligible for an A75 transitional open work permit in Canada, applicants must meet specific criteria, aligned with Canada's economic immigration policies. Here are the main eligibility conditions for this type of permit:

  1. Current permanent residence process: The applicant must have submitted an application for permanent residence under one of Canada's economic immigration categories. This includes programs managed by the Express Entry system, such as the Canadian Experience Class, the Federal Skilled Worker Program, and the Federal Skilled Trades Program, as well as other economic programs.
  2. Valid temporary status: The applicant must currently be residing in Canada with a legal temporary status, either as a temporary worker, foreign student, or under any other temporary status that allows a request for a change of conditions to obtain a work permit.
  3. Application for permanent residence at the decision approach stage: The applicant's application for permanent residence must have reached the stage where a decision is about to be made by Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC). This means that the majority of checks, including security and admissibility checks, have been successfully completed.
  4. No grounds for ineligibility: Applicants must not be deemed ineligible for reasons of safety, criminality or health. They must meet all IRCC's general eligibility requirements.

How and where can I apply for an A75 transitional open work permit?

To apply for an A75 Transitional Open Work Permit, applicants must follow a detailed process and use the resources available from Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC). Here's a step-by-step guide:

  1. Check your eligibility: Make sure you meet the eligibility criteria for the A75 permit, including having a current application for permanent residence in an economic immigration category.
  2. Gather the necessary documents: Collect all required documents, such as proof of your application for permanent residence, proof of legal status in Canada if applicable, and any other documents specified by IRCC.
  3. Complete the application form: Download and complete the IMM 5710 form for changing conditions, renewing your stay or changing the type of work permit in Canada. Select "Open work permit" and indicate exemption code A75.
  4. Fee payment: Pay the processing fee for your open work permit application. Fees can be viewed on the IRCC website and are payable online by credit or debit card.
  5. Submit your request :
  6. Online: Online submission via the IRCC secure account is recommended for a faster procedure. Upload your completed form and supporting documents.
  7. By post: If online submission is not possible, you can also send your application by post to the address indicated by IRCC. Check the submission address and instructions on the IRCC website.
  8. Application tracking: After submission, you can check the status of your application via your IRCC account. IRCC will contact you if additional information is required to process your request.

Accurate and complete information is essential to avoid delays. Check the IRCC website regularly for up-to-date information on procedures and fees, as guidelines may change.

How long is an A75 transitory open work permit valid?

The validity period of an A75 transitional open work permit is generally determined by several factors, but does not exceed 24 months (2 years). This period is designed to allow applicants for permanent residence to continue working in Canada while their application is being processed. Here are the main factors that can influence the length of validity of the A75 permit:

  • The expiry date of the applicant's passport: The permit cannot exceed the validity of the passport. If the passport expires before the maximum period of 24 months, the permit will be granted until the passport expiry date.
  • Application for permanent residence: The A75 permit is specifically intended for individuals with an application for permanent residence in process. The duration of the permit can therefore be adjusted to cover the estimated period of the permanent residence process, without exceeding 24 months.
  • Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) guidelines: IRCC may impose specific limits on permit duration based on current policies and operational needs.

It is important for A75 permit holders to keep an eye on the expiry date of their permit and passport. If their application for permanent residence is still being processed and their permit is about to expire, they may be eligible to apply for a permit extension, depending on IRCC guidelines at the time.

Applicants are encouraged to consult the IRCC website regularly for the latest information on the duration of transitional open work permits and renewal procedures, as policies and procedures may change.

Conclusion

In summary, the A75 Transitional Open Work Permit marks a significant milestone in the journey of candidates for permanent residence in Canada, facilitating a smooth transition to their new lives. By offering the possibility of working for any employer without the need for a Labour Market Impact Assessment (LMIA), this permit underlines Canada's commitment to effectively integrating foreign talent into its economy. For applicants, the A75 permit represents not only a pathway to professional stability during a period of transition, but also recognition of their essential contribution to the diversity and prosperity of the Canadian labour market.

title: Obtaining the A73 work permit in Quebec: A complete guide for CSQ holders
excerpt: In a complex immigration landscape, Canada's A73 work permit is emerging as a valuable avenue for holders of a Certificat de Sélection du Québec…
html:
In a complex immigration landscape, Canada's A73 work permit is emerging as a valuable avenue for holders of a Certificat de Sélection du Québec (CSQ), offering a unique exemption from the Labour Market Impact Assessment (LMIA). Designed specifically for individuals selected by Quebec, this closed work permit, linked to a specific employer, facilitates integration into the Canadian labor market for those awaiting permanent residency. Through this article, we explore the nuances of the A73 permit, detailing its rigorous eligibility criteria, the application process, and how it serves as a bridge between immigration ambition and actual entry into the Quebec workforce. Focusing on the permit's importance to Quebec's economic development and the successful integration of skilled immigrants, we offer an in-depth look at the A73 permit's significant impact on applicants and the Canadian labor market.

What is an A73 work permit in Canada?

The A73 work permit in Canada, while representing a specific exemption from the Labour Market Impact Assessment (LMI) for holders of a Certificat de Sélection du Québec (CSQ), is characterized as a closed work permit. This means that the permit is tied to a specific employer, unlike an open work permit which would allow the holder to work for any employer in Canada. Individuals holding a CSQ, residing in Quebec and being the principal applicants in an application for permanent residence, benefit from the possibility of working in Canada without their employer having to obtain an LMIA thanks to this permit. This exemption, identified by the code A73, is designed to simplify access to the Canadian labor market for qualified candidates selected by Quebec, in recognition of the province's autonomy in immigration matters. The CSQ is awarded to candidates who meet the requirements of Quebec's immigration programs, and the A73 work permit is an additional step to facilitate their integration by allowing legal employment in Canada while their application for permanent residence is being processed. As a closed work permit, the A73 guarantees that the holder will work for the employer specifically approved as part of their application, thus contributing to the targeted and successful integration of skilled immigrants into Quebec society and the job market.

Who is eligible to apply for an A73 work permit?

To be eligible to apply for an A73 work permit in Canada, an individual must meet several specific criteria, aligned with Quebec and federal immigration policies. Here are the main eligibility requirements for this type of permit:

  1. Certificat de Sélection du Québec (CSQ): Applicants must hold a valid CSQ issued by the Ministère de l'Immigration, de la Francisation et de l'Intégration (MIFI) du Québec. This certificate is proof that Quebec has selected the individual for immigration based on criteria such as skills, work experience and language proficiency.
  2. Principal Applicant: The individual must be the principal applicant on an application for permanent residence that is being processed by Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC). They must provide proof that they are the principal applicant.
  3. Specific programs: The CSQ must be issued under a specific program or pilot program for Quebec. For applicants under the Quebec Skilled Worker Program, the CSQ must indicate "Category: Skilled Worker". It may contain no code or the IQ code. For other categories of applicants, the CSQ must include a code specific to section 9 of the CSQ, and the list of acceptable codes is detailed in the official instructions.
  4. Exemption from LMIA: The A73 work permit offers an exemption from the Labour Market Impact Assessment (LMIA), which means that the employer is not required to prove that no Canadians or permanent residents have been found to fill the position offered to the foreign applicant.

These criteria ensure that the A73 work permit is available to skilled immigrants who have been selected by Quebec to contribute to its labour market and society, while awaiting approval for permanent residency. This process reflects Quebec's and Canada's commitment to facilitating the integration of skilled foreign workers and meeting the specific needs of the Quebec labor market.

How do I apply for an A73 work permit?

To apply for an A73 work permit in Canada, candidates must follow a series of structured steps to ensure that their application is complete and compliant with the requirements of Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) and Quebec's Ministère de l'Immigration, de la Francisation et de l'Intégration (MIFI). Here's a step-by-step guide to submitting an A73 work permit application, including the additional step concerning the employer:

  1. Obtain a Certificat de Sélection du Québec (CSQ ): Make sure you have a valid CSQ issued by the MIFI. This document confirms that you have been selected by Quebec for immigration.
  2. Check your eligibility: Make sure you meet the eligibility criteria for the A73 work permit, including being the principal applicant on a current application for permanent residence and having a CSQ specific to certain categories of skilled workers or pilot programs.
  3. Document preparation: Gather all required documents, including your CSQ, proof that you are the principal applicant on a permanent residence application, and any other necessary documentation specified by IRCC for the A73 work permit type.
  4. Creation of the job offer by the employer: The employer must create a job offer in the IRCC employer portal and pay the associated compliance fees. It is crucial to clearly indicate the A73 EIMT exemption code in the job offer to link the offer to the specific A73 work permit application.
  5. Completing the application form: Download and accurately complete the application form for a work permit outside Canada (IMM 1295) available on the IRCC website. Be sure to clearly indicate that you are applying for an A73 work permit by quoting the EIMT exemption code A73.
  6. Fee payment: Pay the applicable processing fee for your work permit application. Fees can be paid online at IRCC.
  7. Submitting your application: You can submit your application online or on paper, whichever you prefer. For online submission, create an account or log in to your existing account on the IRCC website to upload your forms and supporting documents.
  8. Wait for the decision: Once you have submitted your application, wait for IRCC's decision. You may be asked to provide additional information or undergo a medical examination. IRCC will inform you of the decision regarding your A73 work permit application.

How long is an A73 work permit valid?

The validity period of an A73 work permit in Canada is generally aligned with the duration of the job offer provided by the employer, up to a maximum of two years. However, it can be influenced by a number of factors, including the expiry date of the applicant's passport, the specificity of the immigration program under which the Certificat de Sélection du Québec (CSQ) was issued, and specific conditions imposed by Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) or the Ministère de l'Immigration, de la Francisation et de l'Intégration du Québec.

It is important to note that the A73 work permit is issued under specific circumstances, allowing CSQ holders already residing in Quebec to work while they await approval of their application for permanent residence. This specific permit facilitates the integration of skilled workers by meeting both the needs of the Quebec labor market and the province's immigration objectives.

Holders of an A73 work permit should pay close attention to the validity dates of their permits to ensure that they maintain their legal status in Canada. If an extension is required, applicants should start the renewal process well in advance of the expiry of their current permit, providing the necessary supporting documents and, if applicable, a new valid job offer.

Conclusion

In short, the A73 work permit is a key pillar in the journey of skilled immigrants to Quebec, marking a crucial step in their economic and social integration into Canada. Through a detailed exploration of its eligibility requirements, the application process, and its pivotal role in linking immigration ambitions to professional integration, this article highlights the importance of the A73 permit. Designed to simplify access to the job market for those already chosen by Quebec, the A73 permit not only facilitates the transition to permanent residency, but also reinforces Quebec's autonomy in immigration matters. It underscores Canada's and Quebec's commitment to welcoming and integrating foreign talent, thereby contributing to a dynamic and diverse labour market. In conclusion, the A73 work permit embodies a valuable opportunity for CSQ holders, offering a secure and legal path to employment in Canada, while awaiting finalization of their permanent residency process, reinforcing the interconnection between immigration policies and the needs of the Quebec labor market.

title: How do you prepare for the arrival of a low-wage temporary foreign worker?
excerpt: In Canada, a low-wage temporary foreign worker is defined as a worker who earns less than the provincial median wage for their occupation. These…
html:
In Canada, a low-wage temporary foreign worker is defined as a worker who earns less than the provincial median wage for their occupation. These workers are hired under the Temporary Foreign Worker Program (TFWP). 

The integration of a low-wage temporary foreign worker in Canada represents an essential bridge between the immediate needs of the Canadian labour market and the immense potential offered by international talent. This guide aims to equip employers with all the knowledge and resources they need to facilitate this transition, ensuring that the arrival and integration of these workers takes place under the best possible conditions. From the provision of suitable accommodation to the management of administrative formalities, every step is crucial to ensure not only compliance with legal requirements, but also to support the well-being and productivity of the worker. This process, though complex, is an opportunity to enrich cultural and professional diversity within the Canadian working environment, while meeting specific labor market needs.

Before the temporary foreign worker arrives

1) Ensuring adequate and affordable housing

You must provide the worker you hire with suitable, affordable housing, or ensure that such housing is available.

  • Suitable housing: not in need of major repairs, in the opinion of residents. Major repairs include work to repair plumbing or electrical wiring, or structural work to repair walls, floors or ceilings.
  • Affordable housing: costs less than 30% of pre-tax income. Housing costs include rent and the cost of electricity, fuel, water supply and other municipal services.

2) Organizing transport

One of the key elements to consider is the employer's obligation to provide round-trip airfare for the worker between his or her country of origin and the workplace in Canada. This obligation is designed to ensure that workers can return to their country of origin at the end of their contract. Providing transportation for low-wage temporary foreign workers contributes to a fair and secure hiring experience. It also facilitates the immigration and integration process for the worker. It is important to note that transportation costs should not be recovered from the worker.

3) Take out temporary health insurance

Employers are required to provide temporary health insurance to their temporary foreign workers until they are eligible for the Quebec Health Insurance Plan (RAMQ). This insurance must cover at least emergency medical care. The employer's health insurance coverage must begin on the worker's first day of work in Canada, and costs must not be recovered from the worker.

Best practice: It can take up to 3 months for a worker's claim to be accepted by RAMQ. It is therefore advisable to take out insurance for a period of at least 3 months.

Some companies offering temporary insurance for foreign workers:

  • Desjardins 
  • Blue cross 
  • AGA 

5) Simplify bank account opening

Horizon and Desjardins have partnered to make it easier for newcomers to open a remote bank account, with a welcome offer.  

  1. The worker must complete the following short form: Open an account (desjardins.com).
  2. A Desjardins financial advisor will contact the worker by phone and/or e-mail to open an account. The passport number is required at this stage.
  3. Information about the worker's Canadian account will be sent to him, enabling him to transfer funds before his arrival.
  4. Upon arrival in Canada, workers must finalize the opening of their account by presenting their identification documents (passport, work permit, etc.) to the Desjardins newcomers team either at the Montréal airport or at the Caisse Desjardins - Montréal Centre-ville (1101 Sainte-Catherine West, Montréal, Québec H3B 1H8). The means of payment (debit/credit cards) will then be given to them.

On arrival at the airport: The first step towards a positive relationship

1) Welcoming the worker

Welcoming a new employee often begins at the airport. This first contact is crucial to establishing a positive working relationship. Be sure to coordinate with the worker in advance and provide all the necessary information on the time and place of the meeting, and how to recognize you at the airport. Use a welcome sign with the name of your company or the worker to facilitate the identification process. It's also a good idea for your employer to provide transportation from the airport to your place of residence or work.

2) Ensure compliance of work permits

Before leaving the counter at immigration, the worker must ensure that the position, employer and place of work are correctly indicated on his or her permit. We recommend that workers bring food and water from their country of origin. The wait at immigration can be several hours if there are many applicants on the flight and there is nothing to buy on the spot.

3) Finalize bank account opening

Upon arrival in Canada, workers must finalize the opening of their account by presenting their identification documents (passport, work permit, etc.) to the Desjardins newcomers team either at the Montréal airport or at the Caisse Desjardins - Montréal Centre-ville (1101 Sainte-Catherine West, Montréal, Québec H3B 1H8). The means of payment (debit/credit cards) will then be given to them.

In the first few days after arrival

1) Register with the Régie d'Assurance Maladie du Québec (RAMQ)

Upon arrival in Quebec, workers can register with the Régie d'assurance maladie via the RAMQ website.

He must submit a copy of the following documents:

  • Work Permits
  • Passport
  • Proof of residence
  • Request form
  • Employment contract

2) Obtain Social Insurance Number (SIN)

The Social Insurance Number (SIN) is an essential requirement for working in Canada, including for temporary foreign workers.

To obtain a SIN, locate your nearest Service Canada Centre and go there in person.

Documents required to obtain the SIN: 

  • Valid passport
  • Work permits

3) Ensuring compliance as an employer

As an employer, it is your responsibility to send a copy of the mandatory form reminding him of his rights.

4) Declare the hiring of the temporary foreign worker to CNESST

All employers must comply with the labour standards in force in Quebec and with the provisions of any applicable collective agreements. In addition, under Quebec's Act respecting labour standards, employers must inform the Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST) without delay of the arrival and departure dates of temporary foreign workers, and of the duration of their contract. If the departure date is different from the one specified in the contract, the employer must indicate the new date and the reasons for departure. Please consult the CNESST website for more information: www.cnesst.gouv.qc.ca/. 

5) Keep a record of work permit expiry dates

Should you wish to extend your employment relationship with the foreign worker covered by this LMIA, you must submit a new LMIA application to Employment and Social Development Canada/Service Canada and to the Ministère de l'Immigration, de la Francisation et de l'Intégration at least three months before the expiry date of the permit, and simultaneously submit to the Ministère de l'Immigration, de la Francisation et de l'Intégration a new temporary selection application completed by the foreign worker. That's why it's so important to take note of the expiry date of the temporary foreign worker's work permit.

Conclusion

In conclusion, hosting a low-wage temporary foreign worker represents a unique opportunity for Canadian employers to fill gaps in their workforce while enriching their work environment with new perspectives and skills. However, navigating the hosting process requires careful preparation and attention to detail to ensure that the experience is beneficial and respectful for all parties involved. From arranging housing and transportation to health insurance, opening a bank account and registering with RAMQ, each step is crucial to ensuring a smooth transition for the worker. By respecting these steps, employers not only meet their legal obligations, but also facilitate the worker's integration into the Canadian community and job market. This caring, methodical approach underlines the importance of preparation and support in the successful reception of low-wage temporary foreign workers.

title: How can I get a job in the regions of Quebec as a foreign worker?
excerpt: If you're thinking of immigrating to Quebec, it may be a smart strategy to consider jobs outside the big cities, where the available labor pool is…
html:
If you're thinking of immigrating to Quebec, it may be a smart strategy to consider jobs outside the big cities, where the available labor pool is smaller, to improve your chances of landing a job. Finding a job before you arrive can help you integrate more easily into Quebec society. In this article, we'll guide you through the process of finding a job in the Quebec region from abroad.

1) Research the local job market

The Quebec job market varies considerably from region to region. Some regions have high demand in sectors such as healthcare, education or technology, while others may have more opportunities in agriculture, construction or tourism. Use online resources such as Emploi-Québec or popular job search sites such as Indeed, Jobillico or Emploi en région to find out about jobs available in the regions that interest you.

2) Optimize your CV for the Quebec market

Quebec employers expect a certain CV format and style. Make sure your CV is up-to-date, well-structured and adapted to Quebec standards. Highlight your language skills, especially your command of French, which is a major asset for working in Quebec. See our article on How to optimize your CV for the Quebec job market.

3) Use the most popular online resources

Getting a job from abroad involves using a variety of online resources to search for opportunities, apply for jobs and build relationships with potential employers. Here are the most commonly used online ways to find a job from abroad:

Job boards

Job boards such as Indeed, Glassdoor, Monster, LinkedIn and Jobillico list thousands of vacancies in various fields. These sites allow you to search for jobs by location, industry and level of experience, making it easy to find relevant opportunities.

Specialized job boards

Some sites specialize in specific industries or job types. For example, GitHub Jobs is a great place to search for software development positions, while AngelList is popular for startup jobs.

Company websites

If you have specific companies in mind, check out their websites for dedicated career or employment sections. Many companies publish their job offers on their own website before posting them elsewhere.

LinkedIn

LinkedIn is an essential platform for professional networking and job hunting. In addition to searching for job offers, you can connect with professionals in your industry, follow companies that interest you and participate in relevant discussions. Discover our article on How to get a job with LinkedIn.

Recruitment agencies

Many recruitment agencies operate online, helping employers to fill vacancies. By registering with a recruitment agency, you can access job vacancies that are not always advertised on traditional job boards.

4) Prepare for remote job interviews

Because of the distance involved, most of your interviews will probably be conducted by telephone or video. Be sure to master these interview formats and prepare accordingly. Practice your answers to common interview questions and make sure you have a stable Internet connection for your video interviews.

Conclusion

In short, finding a job in the Quebec region from abroad requires careful preparation and thorough research. By using online resources, optimizing your CV, participating in virtual job fairs, networking, and preparing for long-distance interviews, you can increase your chances of getting a job and thus facilitate your immigration to Quebec.

title: How to optimize your CV for the Quebec job market: Complete guide
excerpt: Optimizing your CV for the Quebec job market is crucial if you're planning to work in this Canadian province. Quebec employers are looking for…
html:
Optimizing your CV for the Quebec job market is crucial if you're planning to work in this Canadian province. Quebec employers are looking for specific CVs that reflect the skills and experience required by the local job market. In this article, we'll give you some practical advice on how to adapt your CV to Quebec standards.

1) Adapt your CV to the Quebec format

Formatting your CV for the Quebec market involves following certain principles and standards specific to this region. Here's how you can format your CV to meet the expectations of Quebec employers:

CV length

Unlike some countries where CVs can be very detailed and lengthy, in Quebec, employers generally prefer one- to two-page CVs. Make sure your CV is concise and contains only the most relevant information.

CV sections

Quebec resumes generally contain the following sections, presented in this order:

  • Header: Include your full name, address, telephone number and e-mail address.
  • Professional objective or career summary: A brief description of your career objectives and what you bring to the company.
  • Work experience: List your previous jobs, starting with the most recent. For each job, indicate the job title, company name, dates of employment and a brief description of your duties and responsibilities.
  • Training: Give details of your diplomas and training courses, starting with the most recent.
  • Skills: List the skills relevant to the position.
  • References: In Quebec, it's customary to include two or three references at the end of your CV.

Style and format

The CV should be clear and easy to read. Use a professional font, such as Arial or Times New Roman, in size 11 or 12. Make sure the formatting is consistent throughout, with clear headings for each section and bullet points to list details. 

Personal information

In Quebec, it is generally inadvisable to include personal information such as age, gender, nationality or marital status in your CV, as it is not relevant to assessing your suitability for the position.

By properly formatting your CV for the Quebec market, you can increase your chances of attracting the attention of employers and landing a job interview.

2) Showcase your language skills

Highlighting your language skills in a CV is crucial, especially if you're applying for a job requiring multilingual skills, or if you're looking for work in a multilingual region like Quebec. Here are a few tips on how to do it effectively:

Create a dedicated section

The best way to highlight your language skills is to devote a specific section to them in your CV. This section can be entitled "Languages" or "Language skills" and should be placed where it will be easily visible, for example near the top of your CV if language skills are particularly important for the job.

Indicate your skill level

It's essential to specify your level of proficiency for each language. You can use the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR), which offers a scale ranging from A1 (elementary user) to C2 (perfect mastery). Another approach is to use terms such as "fluent", "advanced", "intermediate" or "basic" to describe your level.

Be honest

It's important to be honest about your language skills. If you overestimate your skills, it can backfire, especially if the job requires a fluent command of the language.

Mention language certifications

If you have certifications that prove your language skills, such as TCF-Québec for French or TOEFL for English, be sure to mention them. These certifications can give employers a clear idea of your skill level.

Indicate how you used the language

If possible, give concrete examples of how you've used the language in a professional context. For example, if you've translated documents, worked with international customers or conducted meetings in another language, mention it.

By effectively highlighting your language skills on your CV, you can show employers that you have the skills needed to work in a multilingual environment.

3) Customize your CV for each job

Personalizing your CV for each job is an essential practice to increase your chances of being selected for an interview. In Quebec, as in other regions, this means highlighting the skills and experience most relevant to the position in question. Here are a few steps to personalize your CV for each job:

Read the job offer carefully

The first step to personalizing your CV is to read the job offer carefully. Identify the skills and experience required. Identify the keywords used in the ad and note the aspects of the position that match your skills and experience.

Adapt the purpose of your CV

Your CV's objective, or professional summary, is a brief introduction that describes who you are and what you can offer the company. Make sure this objective is tailored to each job you apply for, focusing on your most relevant skills and experience.

Highlight relevant skills

In your skills section, highlight those that are most relevant to the position. For example, if the job posting calls for project management skills, be sure to highlight these skills in your CV.

Adjust the description of your professional experience

For each position you've held, adjust the description of your tasks and responsibilities to highlight the aspects most relevant to the position you're applying for. Use concrete examples to show how you have used your skills in practice.

Use relevant keywords

Be sure to include relevant keywords in your CV that match the job vacancy. This can increase your chances of being selected by the applicant tracking systems used by many companies.

By taking the time to customize your CV for each job, you can show employers that you are a serious candidate who has taken the time to understand the job requirements and show how your skills and experience match those requirements.

Conclusion

Don't forget that your CV is often the first impression you make on a potential employer. Take the time to optimize your CV for the Quebec job market by following these tips. It could mean the difference between landing a job interview or going unnoticed. Good luck in your job search in Quebec!

title: How can we create an inclusive working environment for foreign workers?
excerpt: Globalization and increasing labor mobility mean that more and more companies are opting to recruit temporary foreign workers. These employees bring…
html:
Globalization and increasing labor mobility mean that more and more companies are opting to recruit temporary foreign workers. These employees bring a wealth of skills and perspectives, but it's essential to create an inclusive working environment to maximize the benefits. In this article, we'll give you some practical advice on how to create a corporate culture that values diversity and promotes inclusion.

Training and awareness-raising

Educate management team and existing employees

The first step towards an inclusive environment is to ensure that your management team and employees are aware of inclusion and diversity issues. Here are some strategies for achieving this goal:

  1. Seminars and workshops: Organize seminars and workshops on inclusion and diversity. Invite experts in the field to discuss the benefits of an inclusive environment and offer practical advice.
  2. Online training: Use online training modules that address diversity and inclusion. These modules allow management team members to complete the training at their own pace.
  3. Case studies: Present case studies of other companies that have successfully created inclusive work environments, and discuss their benefits and challenges.
  4. Regular meetings: Incorporate discussion of diversity and inclusion into regular management team meetings. This will encourage open dialogue and ongoing reflection on the subject.
  5. Employee feedback: Share testimonials and experiences of employees who have benefited from an inclusive work environment.

Policies and procedures

Establish clear rules

Implement anti-discrimination and harassment policies to ensure that all employees are treated with respect and dignity, whatever their cultural or national origin.

  1. Simple, clear language: Use simple, direct language so that everyone can understand.
  2. Specificity: Be as specific as possible. Define what constitutes inclusive and non-inclusive behavior.
  3. Setting limits: Make it clear what is not acceptable, and what the consequences will be for non-compliance.

Complaint channels

Create safe, anonymous communication channels where workers can report any form of discrimination or harassment without fear of repercussions. Establish a clear process for reporting violations of inclusion rules. Ensure that employees who report problems are not penalized.

Recruitment and integration

Fair recruitment process

Use recruitment methods that eliminate unconscious bias, such as diverse interview panels and neutral hiring criteria. For example, use

  1. Neutral language: Use neutral language in job ads to avoid discouraging specific groups from applying.
  2. Resume anonymization: Remove names and other personal identifiers from resumes to reduce bias related to ethnic origin, gender, age, etc.
  3. Standardized evaluation grid: Use a grid to evaluate candidates' skills and qualifications objectively.
  4. Structured interviews: Prepare a standard list of questions to ensure that every candidate is assessed in the same way.
  5. Objective evaluation criteria: Establish clear, measurable evaluation criteria to compare candidates objectively.
  6. Collective evaluation: Involve several people in the evaluation process to balance perspectives and minimize bias.

Conclusion

Recruiting temporary foreign workers offers many benefits to companies, from diversifying skills to boosting productivity. However, to make the most of them, it's crucial to create a working environment that's not only welcoming but also inclusive. By investing in training, policy adaptation and flexibility, you can build a corporate culture that fosters diversity and inclusion.

title: International recruitment in Quebec: Strategies and benefits for Quebec companies
excerpt: In today's business world, international recruitment has become a key strategy for many companies. Due to the labor shortage in Quebec, this trend is…
html:
In today's business world, international recruitment has become a key strategy for many companies. Due to the labor shortage in Quebec, this trend is also on the rise, with more and more companies looking to attract international talent. This article will focus on international recruitment in Quebec, the benefits it offers local companies and best practices for a successful recruitment strategy.

Why is international recruitment essential to Quebec?

Quebec is a dynamic province with a thriving economy. However, with low unemployment and a shortage of talent in many sectors, Quebec companies are increasingly turning to international recruitment to fill the gaps. International recruitment is essential in Quebec for several key reasons:

  1. Filling skills gaps: Certain sectors of the Quebec economy, such as information technology and healthcare, are facing a shortage of qualified talent. International recruitment enables companies to fill these gaps by accessing a larger, more diversified pool of talent.
  2. Stimulate innovation: Hiring international talent can bring new perspectives and ideas, which can stimulate innovation and creativity within companies.
  3. Meeting the demographic challenge: With an aging population and a low birth rate, Quebec faces a demographic challenge. International recruitment can help alleviate this problem by attracting a young, dynamic workforce.
  4. Enhancing diversity: International recruitment can help to increase cultural diversity within companies, which in turn can improve performance and strengthen the company's ability to operate in international markets.
  5. Stimulate economic growth: By attracting international talent, Quebec can boost its economic growth and strengthen its competitiveness on the world stage.

What are the advantages of international recruitment for companies?

International recruitment is an essential strategy for Quebec companies seeking to grow, innovate and remain competitive in today's global economy. International recruitment offers several significant advantages for Quebec companies:

  1. Access to a large talent pool: International recruitment opens doors to a vast talent pool, enabling Quebec companies to attract professionals with diverse skills and experience that may not be available locally.
  2. Cultural diversity: Employing international workers enhances cultural diversity within the company. This diversity can stimulate innovation, improve problem-solving and foster a better understanding of international markets.
  3. Workforce succession: With an aging population and labor shortages in certain sectors, international recruitment can help to ensure workforce succession.
  4. Competitiveness and economic growth: Attracting international talent can stimulate economic growth and strengthen the competitiveness of Quebec companies in the global marketplace.

What are the best practices for international recruitment in Quebec?

Here are some best practices for successful international recruitment in Quebec:

  1. Knowledge of laws and regulations: Understanding Quebec and Canadian immigration and employment laws and regulations is crucial. This includes processes for obtaining work permits, validating foreign qualifications and complying with labor standards.
  2. Working with reputable recruitment partners: Working with international recruitment agencies or immigration consultants can facilitate the recruitment process and ensure compliance with laws and regulations.
  3. Francization program: Your company may benefit from assistance in setting up in-house French language training. A number of French-language training options are available for companies wishing to promote the linguistic integration of their immigrant employees who are not French-speaking, or who speak French only to a limited extent. Under certain conditions, these courses can be offered at no cost to the company. Services Québec and MIFI cover the costs of these courses, and coordinate their implementation for companies that express the need.
  4. Offering support programs: Offering support programs to facilitate the relocation and integration of international employees can be a key factor in attracting and retaining international talent. This can include relocation assistance, language training, cultural integration programs, etc. Approximately one hundred community organizations provide assistance to new arrivals to facilitate their integration process in Quebec. Consult the directory to find organizations in your area.
  5. Creating an inclusive work environment: Providing an inclusive and culturally diverse work environment can help retain international talent over the long term. Here are a few examples: Establishing clear policies on inclusion and diversity. For more information, read our article.

Conclusion

International recruitment is a key strategy for many Quebec companies seeking to boost their growth and competitiveness. By adopting a strategic approach and offering ongoing support to international employees, Quebec companies can attract and retain top talent from around the world.

title: The Global Talent Stream: A fast-track to a Canadian work permit
excerpt: The Global Talent Stream (GTS) is positioning itself as a key program for stimulating growth and innovation in Canada. This article will examine how…
html:
The Global Talent Stream (GTS) is positioning itself as a key program for stimulating growth and innovation in Canada. This article will examine how the Global Talent Stream works, its benefits and its potential impact on your organization.

What is the Volet des Talents Mondiaux (VTM)?

The Global Talent Stream is an initiative designed to assist companies in the temporary immigration of the world's most talented and highly skilled workers. It aims to speed up the immigration process for skilled foreign workers to meet labor market needs in specific sectors, often in the fields of technology, science and engineering.

The program enables companies to recruit these workers through an accelerated process, helping to fill skills gaps and stimulate innovation. Workers who qualify for this program have the opportunity to receive their work permit more quickly, which can be a major asset for companies looking to attract international talent.

The global talent section is divided into two categories:

Category A: Designated recommendation partners

Category A requires a recommendation from one of the Canadian government's designated partners. These partners are generally organizations that support innovation in Canada.

To be eligible for this category, the employer must hire a unique and specialized talent that is considered essential to the company. The position offered must be in an occupation where there is a labour shortage in Canada.

Category B: List of professions in demand

Category B does not require designated partners. Instead, this category focuses on a list of in-demand professions that are considered crucial to Canada.

To be eligible for Category B, the employer must offer employment in an occupation that appears on the List of Occupations Requiring Global Talent. This list may change over time, depending on economic and labor market needs.

Common requirements:

In addition to the criteria specific to each category, there are common requirements that must be met. These requirements may include, but are not limited to:

  • Engage in activities that promote skills development and training for Canadians.
  • Offer competitive wages and working conditions in line with Canadian standards.
  • Pay costs associated with the process, including employer compliance fees.

What are the advantages of the Volet des Talents Mondiaux (VTM)?

The Global Talent Stream offers many advantages, but here are the three main ones:

  1. Accelerated process: The process of obtaining a work permit is significantly faster with this program, usually completed in just two weeks. This is a significant advantage for companies needing to fill specialized positions quickly, as well as for foreign workers wishing to establish themselves quickly in their new country.
  2. Dedicated support: Employers participating in the VTM benefit from a dedicated support service from Employment and Social Development Canada (ESDC), which helps them navigate the application process and answer their specific questions.
  3. Stimulating innovation: By attracting global talent, companies can increase the diversity of their teams, which has been shown to stimulate innovation. Foreign workers can bring new perspectives and ideas, which can lead to significant breakthroughs and company growth.

What is a Labour Market Benefits Plan (LMBP)?

The Labour Market Benefits Plan (LMBP) is an essential component of the Global Talent Stream (GTS). It is an employer's commitment to the Canadian government to contribute to the long-term growth of the Canadian workforce.

When an employer wishes to hire a foreign worker through the Global Talent Stream, it must develop and submit a Labour Market Benefits Plan, which details the specific investments and activities the employer will undertake to train and develop the Canadian workforce. The aim is to ensure that the hiring of foreign workers translates into long-term benefits for the Canadian labour market.

Here are some key elements of the Labour Market Benefits Plan:

  1. Complementary investments: Employers must commit to investing in the training and development of Canadians and permanent residents, in addition to any training expenses related to the hiring of a foreign worker.
  2. Concrete activities: The plan must include specific, measurable activities that the employer commits to carrying out. This can include things like apprenticeship programs, internships, investments in employee training, and more.
  3. Consultation with the Ministry: The plan is developed in consultation with Employment and Social Development Canada (ESDC) to ensure that it meets the requirements and needs of the labour market.
  4. Monitoring and compliance: The employer must adhere to the agreed plan and report regularly on progress. There may be audits to verify compliance.
  5. Flexibility: The plan must be adapted to the employer's needs and capabilities, and may vary according to company size and industry.

In short, the Labour Market Benefits Plan aims to ensure that hiring global talent contributes to the growth and development of Canadian skills. It demonstrates a balanced approach to hiring foreign talent, ensuring that the benefits are not just short-term for the employer, but long-term for the Canadian labour market as a whole.

Conclusion

The Global Talent Stream is more than just an immigration initiative - it's a powerful engine for growth and innovation. By leveraging VTM, your organization can access a global talent base, drive innovation and fill skills gaps.

title: How do I obtain a Temporary Resident Visa (TRV) for Canada?
excerpt: In a global environment where international mobility plays a key role in professional and personal success, Canada is emerging as a preferred…
html:
Ina global environment where international mobility plays a key role in professional and personal success, Canada is emerging as a preferred destination for those looking to enrich their experience abroad. Whether you're planning to work, study or simply visit, obtaining a Temporary Resident Visa (TRV) can be an essential step in your mobility project to Canada. This article aims to provide you with an overview of the process of obtaining a TRV for Canada.

What is a Temporary Resident Visa (TRV)?

The temporary resident visa is an official sticker issued by the Canadian government and placed in a person's passport to prove that he or she meets the requirements for admission to Canada as a temporary resident. This visa is essential for people wishing to visit Canada temporarily and who are citizens of countries subject to visa requirements.

Understandingthe difference between visa and status in Canada

It's essential to make a clear distinction between a Temporary Resident Visa (TRV) and a status in Canada, such as a work permit or study permit, as these terms are often confused. A Temporary Resident Visa (TRV) is a document issued to enter Canada, while work and study permits are statuses granting the right to work or study in the country. A TRV is required for entry into Canada, but does not automatically entitle the holder to work or study, for which specific permits are required. Respecting the validity and conditions of each document is crucial to complying with Canadian regulations.

The different types of TRV

Canada offers various types of Temporary Resident Visa (TRV) to meet the specific needs of visitors. Each type of visa has its own conditions and allows applicants to travel to Canada for specific reasons. Here's an overview of the different types of TRVs available: transit visas, single-entry visas and multiple-entry visas.

Transit Visa

The transit visa is intended for travelers passing through Canada for less than 48 hours en route to another destination. This visa is required for individuals who do not qualify for a visa waiver or an ETA (Electronic Travel Authorization), and who are transiting Canada by air. Applicants must provide proof of continued travel, such as an airline ticket to their final destination.

Single-Entry Visa

The single-entry visa allows the holder to enter Canada only once. Once the visitor leaves Canada, except to travel to the U.S. or St. Pierre & Miquelon, he or she must apply for a new visa to return. This type of visa is ideal for short-term visits, such as tourism, visiting family or friends, or business. Applicants must demonstrate their intention to leave Canada at the end of their stay, and prove that they have sufficient funds for their visit.

Multiple-Entry Visa

The multiple-entry visa is the most flexible. It allows the holder to travel to and from Canada for multiple entries for up to 10 years, or up to one month before the passport expires, whichever comes first. This type of visa is preferable for people who plan to visit Canada several times, whether for personal, professional or short-term study reasons.

Conditions of Eligibility

Applicants must :

  • Demonstrate the intention to leave Canada at the end of their authorized stay.
  • Proof of sufficient funds to cover their stay.
  • Not a threat to Canadian security.
  • Be in good health (medical examinations may be required).
  • No criminal record (a police certificate may be required).
  • Be prepared to comply with Canadian laws.

Application process

The application procedure for a Temporary Resident Visa (TRV) to Canada is structured and requires careful attention to detail to ensure a successful submission. Here are the key steps to follow to navigate the application process efficiently.

Preparing your application

  1. Determining the type of visa: First of all, identify the type of visa best suited to your situation (transit, single entry, multiple entry, Super Visa, etc.), taking into account the purpose of your visit.
  2. Gather the required documents: Gather all the necessary documents, which may include a valid passport, proof of sufficient funds, a letter of invitation from someone in Canada, passport-size photos to the required specifications, and other supporting documents specific to your case.

Application submission

  1. Completing application forms: Application forms must be completed accurately. All information provided must be accurate and up-to-date.
  2. Payment of fees: Application fees vary according to visa type, and must be paid at the time of submission. Payment is often made online via the official Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) website.
  3. Online or paper submission: Depending on your application requirements, submit your application online or by mail. Online submission is generally faster and allows easy tracking of your application status.

After Submission

  1. Waiting for processing: Processing times vary according to visa type and visa office. Check the official Government of Canada website regularly for up-to-date processing time estimates.
  2. Interview or Additional Requests: In some cases, you may be called for an interview or asked to provide additional documents.
  3. Decision: You will receive notification of the decision on your application. If approved, you will receive instructions on further procedures, including how and where to collect your visa.

Costs and lead times

The fees associated with the TRV application vary according to the type of visa requested:

  • Processing fee for a visitor visa (single and multiple entries): The standard fee is $100 CAD per person. For families traveling together, a maximum amount may apply.
  • Super Visa processing fee: The cost is $100 CAD, with an additional fee for temporary residency if required.
  • Diplomatic, official, courtesy and facilitation visas: Generally, there are no fees for these categories.

It's important to check the latest information on the official Government of Canada website, as fees may be subject to change.

Processing times

Processing times for TRV applications can vary considerably depending on several factors, such as the applicant's country of origin, seasonality, and the complexity of the application:

  • Visitor visas: Standard processing times can vary from a few weeks to several months.
  • Super Visa: Processing may take a little longer due to additional requirements, such as proof of medical insurance.
  • Diplomatic and official visas: These requests are often given priority and can be completed in a shorter time.

For a more accurate estimate of current processing times, applicants should consult the official Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) website, which provides regular updates.

Other visa categories

The Canadian government offers a variety of visa categories to meet the specific needs of international visitors. Each category is designed to facilitate entry under specific circumstances, ranging from long-term family visits to diplomatic missions. Here's an overview of the visa categories available: Super Visas, Diplomatic and Official Visas, Courtesy Visas, and Facilitation Visas.

Super visas

The Super Visa is specifically designed for parents and grandparents of Canadian citizens or permanent residents of Canada. It allows these relatives to stay in Canada for periods of up to two years at a time, without having to renew their status. To be eligible, it is necessary to provide proof of Canadian medical insurance valid for at least one year, and to pass a medical examination.

Diplomatic and official visas

These visas are intended for foreign diplomats and officials traveling to Canada on official business. This category aims to facilitate international cooperation by offering simplified access to Canada for those representing their government or an international organization.

Courtesy visas

Courtesy Visas are granted to individuals who do not meet the criteria for diplomatic or official visas, but who are of importance to Canada. This includes foreign leaders, members of royal families and other high-ranking personalities visiting for unofficial reasons. The granting of these visas is at the discretion of the Canadian government.

Facilitation visas

Facilitation Visas are issued to Canadian citizens with dual nationality who do not hold a valid Canadian passport but have a passport from another country. This category allows these individuals to enter Canada as citizens, facilitating their return to the country if necessary.

Conclusion

In conclusion, obtaining a Temporary Resident Visa (TRV) for Canada is a crucial step for anyone wishing to explore, work or study in this country rich in opportunity and cultural diversity. Understanding the nuances between a visa and status in Canada, as well as the different types of TRV available, is essential to successfully navigating this process. Clear requirements in terms of eligibility conditions and careful monitoring of the application process increase your chances of a successful Canadian experience. In the event of a refusal, a careful assessment of the reasons and an informed resubmission can open up new avenues. With the right preparation and a thorough understanding of the process, your mobility project to Canada can be a success.

title: All you need to know about the Certificat de sélection du Québec (CSQ)
excerpt: Every year, thousands of people set course for Quebec, attracted by its cultural richness and professional opportunities. Many of them must navigate…
html:
Every year, thousands of people set course for Quebec, attracted by its cultural richness and professional opportunities. Many of them must navigate the process of obtaining the Certificat de Sélection du Québec (CSQ), an essential step for those aspiring to settle permanently in this dynamic Canadian province. The CSQ is not just a document; it's the key to a new life in Quebec, marking the beginning of a promising immigration journey.

What is the Certificat de sélection du Québec (CSQ)?

TheCertificat de Sélection du Québec (CSQ) is a decisive step for those considering Quebec as their place of permanent residence. This official document, issued by Quebec's Ministère de l'Immigration, de la Francisation et de l'Intégration (MIFI), signifies that the holder has been selected by the province to settle there.

The CSQ is not a visa or residence permit; rather, it confirms that the applicant meets Quebec's specific immigration criteria. Having this certificate in hand is essential for most immigrants wishing to settle in Quebec, whether as a skilled worker, an international student with a degree from Quebec, an entrepreneur, an investor, or as part of a family reunion.

The CSQ process evaluates a number of criteria, including mastery of the French language, education, professional experience and ties to Quebec. The aim is to ensure that candidates are able to integrate harmoniously and contribute positively to Quebec society.

Once the CSQ has been obtained, the candidate must then submit his or her application for permanent residency to the Canadian federal government, which will carry out the final verifications, particularly in terms of health and safety.

Why is the CSQ necessary?

Quebec has an agreement with the federal government that allows it to select immigrants according to specific criteria that meet the province's needs and requirements. Eligibility criteria for the CSQ are based on factors such as age, education, work experience, knowledge of French and English, and other factors related to the applicant's ability to adapt and integrate into Quebec society. Without this document, the federal government will not process applications for permanent residence in Quebec.

Who needs a CSQ to immigrate to Quebec?

Skilled workers

People wishing to immigrate to Quebec as skilled workers must obtain a CSQ. This program is aimed at candidates who can contribute to the Quebec economy thanks to their skills, experience and language abilities, particularly in French.

Quebec graduates

Quebec graduates can aspire to stay permanently in the province. To do so, they must go through the Quebec Experience Program (PEQ) and obtain a CSQ.

Entrepreneurs, investors and the self-employed

Those planning to invest, start a business or work for themselves in Quebec must also obtain a CSQ under the programs dedicated to business people.

Sponsored family members

Persons sponsored by a permanent resident or Canadian citizen residing in Quebec must obtain a CSQ to immigrate under the family reunification program.

What are the steps involved in obtaining a CSQ?

One of the key steps in this process is the use of the Arrima platform, an online system designed to simplify and accelerate the processing of Quebec immigration applications, particularly for the Regular Skilled Worker Program (RSWP) and the Quebec Experience Program (QEP). Here's how to navigate the process of obtaining a CSQ, with particular emphasis on using Arrima.

Step 1: Check your eligibility

Before you take the plunge, make sure you meet the eligibility criteria for the immigration program you're applying for. Quebec offers several programs, each with its own requirements in terms of skills, professional experience, education and language proficiency.

Step 2: Create a profile on Arrima

Arrima is an online immigration application management system used by Quebec. The first step is to create an Arrima profile, where you'll provide information about your education, work experience, language skills and other relevant details.

Step 3: Submit your declaration of interest

Once you have completed your Arrima profile, you must submit a declaration of interest. This means you are officially informing Quebec of your desire to become a permanent resident.

Step 4: Receive an invitation and submit a CSQ request

If you are selected through Arrima, you will receive an invitation to submit a formal CSQ application. At this stage, you will be asked to provide additional supporting documentation.

Step 5: Evaluation and decision

Your application will be evaluated according to a number of criteria, including your age, education, work experience and fluency in French. If your application is approved, you will receive your CSQ, marking the successful completion of this crucial step in the Quebec immigration process.

Step 6: Application for permanent residence

With the CSQ in hand, the next step is to submit an application for permanent residence to the Canadian federal government, which will make its own assessments before granting permanent resident status.

How long does it take to obtain a CSQ?

The time it takes to obtain a Certificat de Sélection du Québec (CSQ) can vary depending on several factors, including the immigration program chosen, the complexity of the file and the volume of applications received by Quebec's Ministère de l'Immigration, de la Francisation et de l'Intégration (MIFI). Understanding these deadlines is essential for candidates planning their immigration to this French-speaking province of Canada. In general, CSQ applications via PEQ or PRTQ are processed within 6 months. It is important to note that these times are indicative and may change depending on current immigration policies and the volume of applications.

How much does a CSQ application cost?

As of January 1, 2024, the fees associated with the CSQ application are structured as follows:

For skilled workers and students

  • Principal applicant: The fee for a CSQ application under the Regular Skilled Worker Program (RSWP) and the Quebec Experience Program (QEP) is $895 CAD.
  • Spouse or common-law partner: Adding a spouse or common-law partner to the application will incur an additional fee of $192 CAD.
  • Dependent children: For each dependent child included in the application, the fee is $192 CAD per child.

Other expenses

It is important to note that these amounts represent only the cost of processing the CSQ application. Applicants must also anticipate other costs related to the immigration process, including :

  • Fees for language tests, if required, to demonstrate proficiency in English or French.
  • Costs associated with the collection and official translation of supporting documents.
  • Application fees for permanent residency with Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) once the CSQ has been obtained.

Does the CSQ guarantee permanent residency in Canada?

Once the CSQ has been obtained, the candidate must submit an application for permanent residence to Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC), the federal agency responsible for immigration to Canada. This step, if approved, leads to permanent residency.

Although the CSQ is a necessary condition for candidates wishing to immigrate to Quebec and obtain permanent residency, it does not automatically guarantee this status. Permanent residency is granted after a successful evaluation of the application by IRCC, including security and health checks. The CSQ is therefore an important step towards permanent residency in Quebec, but it must be followed by a successful application to IRCC to achieve the ultimate goal of immigration to Canada.

Can I work in Quebec with a CSQ while waiting for permanent residency?

It's crucial to understand that the CSQ is a selection document issued by Quebec's Ministère de l'Immigration, de la Francisation et de l'Intégration (MIFI), confirming your eligibility to immigrate to Quebec. However, this certificate, while essential, does not directly authorize you to work. To work in Quebec while awaiting permanent residency, you'll need to obtain a valid work permit.

Navigating the Regulations : A73 and A75

Sections A73 and A75 of the Immigration Regulations specify the conditions under which CSQ holders may apply for a work permit. Under these provisions, candidates who have received their CSQ under specific programs may be eligible to apply for a temporary work permit from the federal government, thus facilitating their integration into the Quebec labor market while their application for permanent residence is being processed.

Conclusion

In conclusion, the Certificat de Sélection du Québec (CSQ) represents a key step for those considering a move to the vibrant province of Quebec. As we've explored, the CSQ is much more than just an administrative document; it symbolizes Quebec's approval of your life project, and paves the way for a promising future in this province rich in culture and opportunity.

For accurate and personalized immigration advice, we strongly recommend that you consult a qualified lawyer or immigration consultant.

title: All about the Certificat d'Acceptation du Québec (CAQ)
excerpt: The Certificat d'Acceptation du Québec (CAQ) is required to work or study in Quebec because of the unique immigration arrangement between Quebec and…
html:
The Certificat d'Acceptation du Québec (CAQ) is required to work or study in Quebec because of the unique immigration arrangement between Quebec and the rest of Canada. Quebec has a certain autonomy from the rest of Canada when it comes to immigration. That's why it set up the CAQ system to enable the provincial government to control the number and type of foreign workers and students coming to the province. The CAQ is used to verify that the foreign worker or student meets the conditions required by the province of Quebec.

What is the Certificat d'Acceptation du Québec (CAQ)?

The Certificat d'Acceptation du Québec (CAQ) is an essential document for individuals wishing to settle temporarily in Quebec to study or work. Issued by Quebec's Ministère de l'Immigration, de la Francisation et de l'Intégration (MIFI), the CAQ validates that the bearer has been officially accepted by the province to pursue studies or a professional activity.

Intended primarily for international students and temporary workers, the CAQ is the first step in the immigration process for non-Canadians wishing to reside in Quebec for a specified period. In addition to being a prerequisite for obtaining a study or work permit from the Canadian federal government, the CAQ is a testament to Quebec's commitment to welcoming talent and students from around the world, enriching its community with their diversity and skills.

How do you apply for a CAQ?

To obtain a Certificat d'Acceptation du Québec (CAQ), it's crucial to understand the process specific to each category. The Arrima platform plays an essential role in managing CAQ applications, adapting its approach depending on whether you're a student or a foreign worker.

CAQ application for students

  1. Fill in the online application form for temporary study selection: Fill in the online form on the MIFI website.
  2. Creatingan account on Arrima: International students must first create their own account on Arrima to initiate their CAQ application.
  3. Submit supporting documents: Upload required documents, such as proof of admission to a Quebec educational institution, proof of financial capacity, copies of passport, and transcripts.
  4. Payment of fees: The CAQ application fee must be paid for the application to be processed.
  5. Submission and tracking: Once payment has been made, submit your request and use Arrima to track its progress.

CAQ application for foreign workers

In the case of foreign workers, the employer in Quebec is responsible for filing the CAQ application via Arrima. Here's an outline of the process:

  1. Arrima employer account: Employers must create a specific account on Arrima for companies.
  2. Filing the application: The employer fills out the CAQ application, providing detailed information on the job offer and the foreign candidate, including the nature of the position and the worker's qualifications.
  3. Submission of supporting documents: The employer must also upload the supporting documents needed to back up the foreign worker's application.
  4. Payment of fees: The employer pays the fees for processing the CAQ application on behalf of the foreign worker.
  5. Submission and follow-up: Employers can track the progress of their applications via their Arrima account.

What documents do I need to apply for a CAQ?

To ensure a successful application, it is essential to prepare and submit a complete file including all required documents. Here is an overview of the documents required to apply for a CAQ, tailored to each of these two main categories.

For international students

  1. Proof of admission: Official letter of acceptance from a recognized Quebec educational institution.
  2. Valid passport: A copy of the identification pages of your valid passport.
  3. Proof of funds: Documents proving that you have sufficient financial means to cover your tuition fees, your stay in Quebec and your return travel costs.
  4. Declaration, commitments and authorization form: The official "Declaration, commitments and authorization" form, correctly completed.

For foreign workers

  1. Signed employment contract: An employment contract duly signed by you and your Quebec employer, specifying the terms and conditions of your employment.
  2. Valid passport: A copy of the identification pages of your valid passport.
  3. Up-to-date resume: An up-to-date CV detailing your educational background and professional experience, highlighting your skills in relation to the position offered.
  4. Proof of professional qualifications: Any diploma, certificate or attestation demonstrating your professional qualifications and technical skills, relevant to the position in question, as well as transcripts.
  5. Temporary selection application form: The official "Temporary Selection Application - Temporary Foreign Worker Program" form, correctly completed.
  6. Work certificates: Certificates or letters from your previous employers, confirming your work experience relevant to the position you wish to fill in Quebec.
  7. Previous authorizations to stay in Canada: If applicable, provide copies of your previous authorizations to stay in Canada, such as work permits, study permits or visitor records.

To guarantee the conformity of your CAQ application file, it is imperative that all documents submitted are in English or French. If your original documents are in another language, they must be accompanied by a professional translation, signed and authenticated by a professional translator.

Whatis the processing time for a CAQ application?

Processing times for Certificat d'Acceptation du Québec (CAQ) applications vary depending on the category under which the application is submitted. For international students wishing to study in Quebec, most temporary selection applications are processed within 25 working days. On the other hand, for foreign workers wishing to join the Quebec job market, CAQ applications usually take between 40 and 50 working days to process. These times are indicative and may fluctuate depending on the volume of applications received by the Ministère de l'Immigration, de la Francisation et de l'Intégration (MIFI) du Québec, as well as the completeness and complexity of the files submitted. Applicants are advised to prepare their applications in advance to anticipate these processing times.

How much does a CAQ application cost?

For international students, the CAQ application fee is $128 CAD. This fee covers the processing of the application by the Ministère de l'Immigration, de la Francisation et de l'Intégration (MIFI) du Québec, and must be paid when the application is submitted online via the Arrima platform, or by any other means specified by the MIFI.

As for foreign workers wishing to obtain a CAQ, the applicable fee is also $222 CAD. This fee is required for the evaluation of the CAQ application under the Temporary Foreign Worker Program, and must be paid by the employer or applicant, as the case may be, at the time of application submission.

It is important to note that these amounts are subject to change, and it is advisable to consult the official MIFI website regularly or contact the ministry directly for the most up-to-date and accurate information on CAQ application fees. Preparing your application carefully and ensuring that you follow all the guidelines provided can facilitate your immigration process to Quebec.

In conclusion

The Certificat d'Acceptation du Québec (CAQ) is an essential prerequisite for international students and foreign workers wishing to immerse themselves in Quebec's unique environment. Thanks to its distinct immigration system, Quebec is sure to attract talents and minds that will contribute to the prosperity and diversity of its society. The CAQ process, while rigorous, is a testament to Quebec's commitment to welcoming and successfully integrating every newcomer.
